questions.question: How do I build a wavetable oscillator that fills a table with one cycle of a sine wave when the patch opens and plays it at 220 Hz?
questions.notes: The p_14 patch-eval question. Fills the table on load with a ';'-prefixed sinesum message to a [table] of 512 + 3 points and plays it with [tabosc4~] fed 220 Hz, citing the tabosc4~ page for the guard points and sinesum. Must not leave the sinesum message unrouted or put the frequency in tabosc4~'s creation argument.

questions.question: How big should the table for [tabosc4~] be, and why does it need extra points?
questions.notes: States the documented requirement: a power of two plus three guard points (one at the start, two at the end, wraparound copies), that sinesum/cosinesum write them automatically, and the 512-points-for-up-to-15-partials guidance. Should not invent other sizes.

questions.question: How do I fill a Pd table with a waveform that has several harmonics at different strengths?
questions.notes: Uses the sinesum (or cosinesum) array method with one amplitude per partial, sent to the table when the patch opens, and notes from the tabosc4~ page not to send new sinesum messages while the table is playing — switch tables with 'set' instead.

questions.question: I want to read a wavetable with [phasor~] and [tabread4~] instead of [tabosc4~]. How do I scale the phasor?
questions.notes: Scales the 0-1 ramp from phasor~ by the table length before tabread4~, cites the tabread4~ and phasor~ pages and the book's wavetable-lookup section, and flags any guard-point offset as the answer's own detail if the excerpts do not state it.
